answers.children: Yes — Bearded Collies are good with children when their energetic nature is matched with active play. Their medium build and affectionate temperament let them bounce around with older kids while their herding background sometimes prompts them to nudge or circle smaller children during excitement. The breed’s intelligence helps them learn gentle interactions when given consistent outlets for their boundless enthusiasm. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — Bearded Collies generally get along with other pets thanks to their sociable and affectionate character. Their herding instincts may lead them to circle or nudge smaller animals but high trainability allows owners to channel this behaviour. The breed’s energetic drive means introductions benefit from structured activity that satisfies their working heritage.
answers.exercise: Bearded Collies need at least an hour of vigorous daily exercise. Bred to trot across Scottish highlands herding livestock their stamina remains high so insufficient activity results in restlessness expressed through pacing or chewing household items. Agility work herding trials and long hikes suit their intelligent build and tireless work ethic.
answers.shedding: Yes — Bearded Collies shed moderately with heavier seasonal shedding. Their long double coat tangles easily especially in the shaggy beard and hindquarters trapping loose hair around the house and requiring frequent removal from furniture and clothing. The weather-resistant texture developed for rugged terrain holds dirt that falls out indoors.
answers.hypoallergenic: Bearded Collies have a long double coat that sheds moderately and produces plenty of loose hair and dander around the house. Their shaggy weather-resistant outer layer tangles easily and requires frequent grooming to prevent mats, especially behind the ears and on the legs where the feathering traps debris from their active days. No breed is genuinely hypoallergenic and the Bearded Collie is not among those usually suggested to allergy sufferers. (PawLabs shedding score: 6/10)
answers.training: Bearded Collies are easy to train because of their high intelligence and strong desire to work with people. Their history as Scottish herding dogs gives them focus during tasks but the same energetic drive can produce stubbornness if mental stimulation is absent. Trainability shines in agility or obedience once the breed’s need for purpose is met.
answers.lifespan: Bearded Collies live 12-14 years. Their medium size and working build support this range while the breed’s historical hardiness from Scottish highlands contributes to overall robustness although individual dogs vary. The energetic temperament and need for outlets remain consistent across their adult years.
answers.size: Bearded Collies reach 45-55 lb and stand 20-22 in at the shoulder. Their medium frame carries a substantial shaggy coat that makes them feel larger when they lean affectionately against legs or sprawl across laps. The proportions developed for herding give them an agile yet sturdy presence indoors.
answers.barking: Bearded Collies do not bark excessively. They tend to grumble or woof in a chatty manner when excited or impatient rather than sounding frequent alarms reflecting their heritage as working companions in quiet Scottish crofts. The moderate vocalisations express their affectionate and intelligent personality without becoming disruptive.
answers.apartment: No — Bearded Collies do not suit apartment living well. Their high energy and need for vigorous daily activity combined with a tendency to become restless indoors make settling difficult without ample outlets. The long double coat also adds to indoor maintenance while their enthusiastic movements suit homes with gardens better.
answers.first-time: No — Bearded Collies are not ideal as a first dog. Their high energy can overwhelm novices without proper outlets and their intelligence combined with herding instincts demands consistent training to prevent boredom-driven behaviours such as chewing. The breed’s need for both mental and physical purpose exceeds what many first-time owners anticipate.
